params.body:
From Nightwatch 33, half an hour after it happened: `cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 30002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received` on `services/multicontract/offer`. The requester was **Googlebot**, on the public warranty route (`real-garant.show?view=website`), so this stood as a 500 on a dealer's own website.

Not caused by today's changes: the seal guard from #729 sits above it and passed through, as it should on production. RealGarant was simply silent, for the second time today (#21 was an empty reply).

Two things made it worse than one slow call. **There was no time limit anywhere** in `RealGarantService`, so the default of thirty seconds applied. And `getPrograms` calls once per programme *and* per period while the page renders, so a silent partner did not hold a visitor for thirty seconds but for thirty seconds times the number of programmes.

The controller already knew the right answer. For a failed login it returns an empty 204, with the comment: *"an empty answer tells the page to take the block away."* It just did not know it for a partner that cannot be reached.

- Every call now carries a limit: 5 s to connect, 10 s in total.
- A `ConnectionException` gives that same 204, so the block disappears instead of the page. The first silence ends the loop, so the wait is one limit rather than one per programme.
- Only "cannot reach" is caught. A real refusal from RealGarant still comes through as a failure: silence and rejection are different news.

`R P2-7.9` extended; finding `een-trage-partner-werd-onze-foutbladzijde`.

**What this does not fix**, and the finding says so: that this block calls a partner during a render at all, and that a search engine triggers those calls on a public page. That is work of a different order.

Full suite green, PHPStan clean.
params.title: A slow partner is not our error page
